title: Expert Parallelism (EP) Support for DeepSeek V2 (#12583)

image.build: docker build -t vllm-task:12583 -f tasks/pr_12583/workload/Dockerfile --build-arg VLLM_VERSION= --build-arg BASE_SHA=7940d8a6a7841113c89b168080b51785946f0cdb --build-arg MERGE_SHA=781096e385112f799c2b12a9aa2660b85efaf983 tasks/pr_12583/workload

workload.note: FusedMoE Triton kernel microbench, GPU-only. PR gives no before/after numbers (design doc).

policy.one_run_is: one `docker run` of the workload cmd per arm per repeat (same image, arm tree swapped in by the prelude)

contention_gate.rules: wait while another tenant uses the GPU (>5 % util or a foreign compute process >1 GiB) or the CPU (load1 > nproc/2)

arm_isolation.tree: wipe the wheel's vllm/*.py, copy the arm's vllm/ over site-packages (compiled .so stay)
arm_isolation.files: overlay ONLY metadata.json:source_files from the arm over the wheel's own tree
arm_isolation.tests_benchmarks: copied from the PR's merge tree to /t without a sibling vllm/ package

policy.noise_model: measure.py: paired log-speedup, MAD sigma, theta = clip(k*sigma, theta_min, theta_max) with k/theta from config.yaml:measure

reported.gain_evidence: I noticed that after enabling EP on a 16-card setup, the time taken for the all-reduce kernel has doubled, and the throughput has dropped by 30%.
reported.experiments_note: FusedMoE Triton kernel microbench, GPU-only. PR gives no before/after numbers (design doc).

standalone.run_baseline: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/tasks/pr_12583:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=baseline vllm-task:12583 -lc 'A=/base; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --model mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 --tp-size 2 --dtype auto --seed 0'
standalone.run_pr_solution: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/tasks/pr_12583:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=pr_solution vllm-task:12583 -lc 'A=/gold; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --model mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 --tp-size 2 --dtype auto --seed 0'
standalone.note: The image already holds both trees (/base = baseline commit, /gold = the PR's merge commit); the one-liner swaps the chosen tree over the installed wheel exactly like run_one.sh's prelude, then runs the workload cmd from /t (the merge tree's tests/ + benchmarks/). NOT PINNED: no tasks/pr_<n>/metadata.json:wheel, so the Dockerfile installs the latest PyPI vLLM (compiled ops may not match either tree) and run_one.sh falls back to source mode (Dockerfile.gpu from a host clone). Pick the first PyPI release after merge_sha and record it as metadata.json:wheel before trusting numbers from this image.
